get.description:
Episode stills and titles plus a wide picture, from ani.zip. Separate from the details so
the page never waits on it; empty when ani.zip has nothing or is down.

Which sources can play this title. Separate from the details so a slow scraper never
holds the title page back.

post.description: What the phone shows before asking "Sign in this TV?".

get.description: Open to a locked TV: it asks this to know whether to show the PIN screen.

post.description: The TV page locks itself when it opens, goes to the background or sits idle.

put.description:
Add or change the PIN from a TV. A TV with a PIN must give the current one; a TV with
none must give the account password, so whoever holds the remote cannot lock the owner out.

get.description: What friends finished watching lately; friends who keep it private are left out.

post.description: Asks to be friends. If they already asked you, this accepts their request.

delete.description: Declines a request sent to you, or takes back one you sent.

get.description: MAL's genres are shared by anime and manga, ids included.

One page image, by a link that `pages` signed. The link names the reader and their
login session and expires, like a stream link; the picture is kept on disk for the next
reader. Only public hosts are fetched (never anything on our own network).

The chapter list, with where the user is in each chapter. Separate from the details so
a slow source never holds the title page back. Every enabled source is asked at once; the
language menu is the union of what they have and the list comes from one source: the one
asked for, else the one with the most chapters in the language (ties go to the earlier one).

delete.description: Hide a title from Continue reading. Progress is kept; reading it again brings it back.

get.description:
The page links of one chapter, plus its neighbours in the same language. The source's
page links are short-lived, so they are resolved here, when the reader opens the chapter.

post.description: Replaces all backup codes, used or not.
Starts enrolment with a fresh secret. Nothing changes for logins until /enable.

delete.description: Back to the default: the linked MAL picture, or the user's initial.

put.description:
Sets the picture from the raw image bytes (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 2 MB). The server
crops it to a square and stores a 256 px WebP.

Registers this device. Sending the same endpoint again updates it, and a device that was
signed in as someone else moves to the current user.

post.description: Sends a sample message to every device the user registered.

get.description:
Finds someone by exact username. Name and picture are public to members, so a request can
go to the right person.
A profile is for the person and their friends only; anyone else gets a 403.

put.description: Remembers the source and sub/dub the user picked for this title.

get.description:
Without `u`, the master playlist of the episode the token is for (with `subs`, listing
its subtitles in the playlist, `sub` being the one to show, for players that fetch it
themselves). With `u`, one
playlist, segment, subtitle or image that an earlier response linked to. Neither needs a
login header: the token or the link names the user and the session, and is checked against
both.

Every source and sub/dub that lists this episode, in fallback order, for the player's
source menu. A source that is slow or failing is left out. Kept for a few minutes per
episode, so reopening the menu or the player doesn't ask every source again.

get.description: The server's clock, so viewers can line their own up with it. Declared before /{code}.

Server-sent events: `state` (the whole room), `playback`, `chat`, and every few seconds
`tick` with the current playback version and snapshot revision. Opening this joins the
room; closing it leaves.

post.description: Invites a friend to a room you are in. They get a notification.

put.description: The host switches everyone to another source, or between sub and dub.

get.description:
Opening, ending and recap times from AniSkip for a copy `length` seconds long. The
player asks once it knows the length, and fills in what the source didn't give.

post.description:
A fresh link to start the episode a /play answer picked (`source` and `lang` are the
ones it reported). Asking costs nothing upstream: the stream is only looked up when the
link is opened. Used to hand the stream to a device that fetches it itself, such as an
AirPlay receiver, long after the first link has expired.

parameters.description: Check the stream again instead of trusting a recent check
parameters.name: fresh

schema.title: Fresh

post.description:
Resolves an episode in the background so pressing play on it later hits warm caches:
the title page asks for the episode its Play button opens, the player for the next one.
Answers at once; nothing is returned and failures are only logged.
